mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive quarters signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < 0 for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarters of YoY decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL over a quarter indicates a restrictive monetary policy is successfully cooling inflation, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls in the same quarter
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls in the same quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a flat unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals labor market tightness without wage inflation, which boosts corporate profit margins and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month MA AND UNRATE flat for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive under the described PAYEMS and UNRATE conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based deterioration in demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2% for at least one year) combined with rising real personal savings (implied by RSAFS growth) signals a prolonged accommodative monetary environment with elevated household savings, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for at least one year AND RSAFS rising YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 2% for one year and RSAFS is rising YoY.
